subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-requestable quarantined execution as a public Plugin SDK/runtime contract, and what concrete security guarantees should that contract make?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the permanent API shape changes security boundaries and public Plugin SDK expectations, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep As Design Item
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define the isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Primitives
options.body: Defer the hook directive and document current sessions_spawn sandbox patterns as the supported workaround for trusted operators.

options.title: Close As Out Of Scope
options.body: Reject plugin-requestable trust-boundary execution if maintainers decide strong isolation must stay at separate gateway or OS-host boundaries.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define the isolation semantics, trust metadata, prerequisite hook context, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is recent ownership of subagent context/thread behavior and the security-sensitive runtime seam this proposal would extend.
